subject: Capacity run-rate & autoscale matrix for GalacticSoft Dedicated deal
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@galacticsoft.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Fernandez <cto@galacticsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity for GS - Q1 run-rate + burst needs

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo. We're excited to progress the Dedicated procurement for GalacticSoft. Two asks as we start the contract conversation:

1) We need a capacity matrix showing steady state run-rate (GPU-hours / vGPU footprint) by environment (prod/staging) and a clear description of how Redwood handles short-term bursts (e.g., traffic spikes during product launches).
2) A proposal for autoscaling policy options (headroom %, cooldowns, pre-warm behavior) and how those map to expected latency / cost tradeoffs.

Timing: our Q1 launch window is mid-Feb; would like a concrete numbers spreadsheet and suggested MA plan to attach to procurement by next week.

Attached: none yet — I can share our internal Q4 forecast if helpful.

Cheers,
Sanjay
VP, Platform Engineering
GalacticSoft
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@galacticsoft.com>
Cc: Marta Fernandez <cto@galacticsoft.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity for GS - Q1 run-rate + burst needs

Sanjay — thanks, this is exactly the right framing. We're happy to produce a capacity matrix + 2-3 autoscale policy options you can include in procurement.

Quick asks before we model numbers:
- Expected steady concurrent requests at peak (tokens/sec or active sessions) for prod and staging.
- Typical request type: short chat (<=256 tokens) vs long generation (>=1024 tokens).
- SLA target for 95th percentile latency (ms) and acceptable cold-start window.

If you can share the Q4 forecast file, we will ingest it into our sizing template. I'll pull Karthik and Laura in to build the matrix and a short runbook describing failover to hosted fallback capacity.

Proposed next step: 30-min sizing sync tomorrow (Mon) at 10am PT?

Best,
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
(415) 555-0194
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 11:25:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity for GS - sizing inputs + first-pass matrix

Forwarding Sanjay's note and dropping an initial sizing matrix for review. Attachments: capacity_matrix_v1.csv, cost_sensitivity.pdf

Summary of assumptions in this draft:
- Prod steady state: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs (single-model footprint), avg concurrency 120 active sessions, median request length ~400 tokens.
- Staging: 1 GPU reserved.
- Burst profile: 2x concurrency for up to 20 minutes on campaign days. We propose a policy that allows ephemeral burst pool allocation (ephemeral spot-equivalent instances) with pre-warm for the most common model variant.

Matrix (excerpt):
- Option A (Conservative): Reserved prod 8 GPUs, staging 1, burst headroom 25% (managed by pre-warm). Estimated cost: $XXk/mo.
- Option B (Balanced): Reserved prod 6 GPUs, staging 1, burst headroom 50% using ephemeral pool + autoscale cooldown 90s. Estimated cost: $YYk/mo.
- Option C (Aggressive burst): Reserved prod 4 GPUs + dedicated ephemeral pool for 2x bursts, cooldown 30s, requires acceptance of slightly higher cold-start risk for non-prewarmed variants. Estimated cost: $ZZk/mo.

Questions for Monica/Laura:
- Do we want to include an SLA tier where Redwood guarantees <150ms 95th at Option B? That would require additional reserved capacity.
- Is Galactic comfortable with ephemeral spot-backed GPUs for burst, or do they require only reserved-backed bursts?

Please review the CSV and cost sensitivity PDF. I'll be at the 10am sync to walk through the numbers.

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@galacticsoft.com>, Marta Fernandez <cto@galacticsoft.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed capacity & autoscale policy options for GalacticSoft (attached matrix)

Hi Sanjay & Marta — thanks for the quick sync earlier. Attached is the capacity_matrix_v1.csv and a short runbook excerpt. High level recommendations below:

Option B (Recommended): Balanced reserved + ephemeral burst
- Reserved: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs for prod, 1 for staging.
- Burst: Ephemeral pool scaled to 3 additional GPUs (approx. 50% headroom) with pre-warm for primary model variant.
- Autoscale policy: target utilization 65%, scale-out threshold 72% sustained for 45s; scale-in cooldown 90s.
- Cold-start mitigation: prefix KV caching and model-variant pre-warm for top 3 routes; fallback to hosted API for non-critical flows.
- Expected 95th p latency: ~120-170 ms under Option B depending on request mix.

Option tradeoffs:
- Option A (higher reserved): better latency guarantees, higher fixed cost.
- Option C (sparse reserved + large ephemeral): lower fixed cost, higher cold-start variance and complexity for pre-warm orchestration.

Next steps we propose for procurement package:
1) Attach capacity_matrix_v1.csv (numbers + cost sensitivity).
2) Mutual Action Plan (MOP) with milestones: PO signed -> Dedicated seat delivery -> Load test -> Pre-warm run -> Production cutover.
3) If you confirm Option B, we'll draft an SLA addendum with expected latency bands and the autoscale parameters included as enforcable runbook items.

Attachments: capacity_matrix_v1.csv (spreadsheet), cost_sensitivity.pdf (one-pager).

Let us know if you want Redwood to commit to reserved-backed bursts (higher cost) vs ephemeral (cost-efficient). Happy to align on the MOP language for procurement.

Warmly,
Monica Patel
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@galacticsoft.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marta Fernandez <cto@galacticsoft.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposed capacity & autoscale policy options for GalacticSoft (attached matrix)

Monica — thanks for the clear options and the matrix. We reviewed with the execs this morning and we're comfortable moving forward with Option B. A few quick confirmations:

- We'll share our Q4 forecast (attached: galactic_q4_forecast.xlsx) so you can finalize numbers.
- For procurement we prefer the MOP language to call out reserved-backed bursts for any times we exceed 75% of reserved capacity for longer than 30m — we can accept ephemeral for short spikes <30m.
- Please prepare the SLA addendum draft and the MOP for signature; we'll aim to return the signed MOP by end of next week.

I've attached the forecast and a signed preliminary MOP (signed_mop_v1.pdf) for your review.

Sanjay Rao
VP, Platform Engineering
GalacticSoft
